title: Per-domain calibration anchor sets for quantization profile validation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible, domain-partitioned set of calibration "anchors" to validate model accuracy regressions introduced by FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. Anchors are compact representative prompt/response pairs and metadata slices sampled from production traffic and augmented to cover rare tokens and edge behaviors. Objective is to produce per-domain anchor sets that are small enough for fast offline calibration + quant-accuracy checks and large enough to surface regressions that matter to end users.
proposed_solution: 1) Partition production prompts into stable domains via tag metadata and prompt fingerprint clustering. 2) For each domain produce two calibration anchor sets: one FP8-focused and one INT8-focused, each with explicit constraints for token-length distribution, function-call presence, and distribution tail coverage. 3) Sampling combines reservoir sampling (bounded memory) with weighted recency and stratified fingerprint quotas. 4) Add synthetic adversarial variants and rare-token upsampling for tokens with >0.1% of regression risk in prior PQAs. 5) Store anchors as lightweight records (prompt, ground-truth response, trace metrics, and fingerprint). 6) Provide tooling to replay anchors against new quant builds and generate per-anchor delta reports for token-level divergence and downstream metric regressions.
sampling_plan:
- Domain identification: use existing domain tags + clustering on prompt fingerprints (SimHash + TF-IDF) to split ambiguous flows.
- Reservoir sampling window: keep a sliding 90-day window with reservoir size per domain = max(500, min(2000, round(0.002 * daily_volume))).
- Stratification slices: token-length buckets (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024), function_call flag, top-500 intents, and fingerprint clusters. Ensure each slice has a minimum quota.
- Weighting: combine recency weight (half-life 21 days) and error-exposure weight (past-regression occurrences).
- Augmentation: for slices with <5% tail coverage synthesize paraphrases via beam-search templates and insert rare tokens sampled from Byte-Pair Encoding rare token inventory.
- Final dedup filter: drop >0.9 similarity duplicates using fuzzy edit + semantic cosine threshold.
- Output: two ndjson files per domain: anchors_fp8.ndjson and anchors_int8.ndjson, each ~1-3k records depending on domain volume.
validation_plan:
- Baseline: run anchors against reference float32 model to compute golden token-level logits and downstream metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, task-specific scores).
- For each quant build (FP8, INT8): replay anchors and compute per-anchor token divergence, logit-shift histograms, and delta on downstream scores.
- Acceptance thresholds: mean token-level KL <=0.02 for FP8 and <=0.05 for INT8; 95th-percentile token divergence under delta thresholds; task score drop <=1.5% relative for FP8 and <=3.5% for INT8.
- Flagging: anchors with >3x regression on any metric become triage items. Aggregate daily regression dashboard and per-domain digest.
- Statistical significance: bootstrap sampling (n=1000) to ensure regressions are not due to sampling variance.
- Regression investigation: link to example traces, model inputs, and failing tokens for kernel-level triage.
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline produces per-domain anchors_fp8.ndjson and anchors_int8.ndjson on a daily cadence
Anchor sets cover token-length and function-call stratification quotas for >=95% domains
Calibration replay job runs in <=12 minutes for median domain and produces delta report artifact
Regression thresholds (KL and downstream score) implemented and integrated with alerting
Documentation and runbook published in Confluence with replay command examples and interpretation guide
rollout_notes: Phase 1: generate anchors for top 20 revenue domains and validate against last 6 quant builds. Phase 2: expand to all domains above 1k daily requests. Phase 3: upstream into CI so candidate quant builds must pass anchor regression gating for release. Keep FP8 and INT8 checks separate and allow opt-out for low-volume internal domains.
